judgments.reasoning_cat1: The preamble treats "Fund" and "Plan" as a single label for the same entity and lists five named individuals as Trustees, wording that is loose but not internally ambiguous on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 1 separately defines "Plan" (1.20, the rules) and "Trust Fund" (1.22, the assets), so the preamble's equation of the two is in tension with the definitional scheme, and Amendment No. 4 replaces the trustee list entirely.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short recital reciting that the CBAs 'establish the Plan' and require periodic contributions; nothing in the wording carries two meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.20 and 4.2 make the Plan a document adopted by the Board rather than something established by the CBAs, a mild recital-versus-operative divergence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely narrative recital that the CBAs contemplate execution of a trust agreement and appointment of Trustees; no term to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 3.1/3.3 (Association and Union select Trustees); I found no operative provision it contradicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recital states an 'exclusive purpose of providing pension and retirement benefits' to 'certain employees', with 'certain' left undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2 and 4.1(a) broaden the purpose to 'pension and related benefits' and 'such other related benefits as the Board may determine', so recital and operative text do not point in exactly the same direction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A factual recital of the Trustees' desire to amend and restate the 1956 instrument; nothing operative or vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 10.1's amendment power; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recital cites 'Paragraph 18 of the Trust Agreement' as the amendment authority, a citation that cannot be matched to anything in the restated text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The operative amendment power is Section 10.1 (and 7.2(1)), so the recital's authority reference is orphaned — a classic recital-versus-operative mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard consideration language ('promises', misspelled as 'promises/prom-ises') with no operative content to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in the instrument turns on it; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'unless the context otherwise requires' opener is a standard escape hatch that in principle lets defined terms float, but it is boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Section 12.7 (Plan definitions control 'except as otherwise expressly provided'), a mild layering of definitional priority rules.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Administrator' means the Board or any person the Board authorizes — circular but workable and clearly bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.1's opening sentence is garbled ('Where the Administrator is a Trust Fund'), leaving the Administrator's role imperfectly meshed with this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A self-referential definition of the instrument itself; no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the preamble and 12.17; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition names the 'Publishers' Association of New York', dropping 'City' from the entity's actual name used everywhere else.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble, Section 12.8(d) and the signature block all say 'Publishers' Association of New York City', so the defined term does not match the party as elsewhere identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'both the Chairman and Secretary of the Board' leaves open whether they must act jointly, while the phrase then sweeps in 'any individual Trustee' duly authorized.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.15 gives the Chairman and Secretary joint execution authority and 12.6 makes instruments signed by the Chairman alone conclusive, a small mismatch about single-signature authority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Beneficiary is defined by reference to the Plan's own terms; a bounded, conventional definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the preamble's use of 'Beneficiaries' and with 12.15/12.16; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Board' is defined with statutory cross-references to ERISA's 'named fiduciary' and 'administrator'; clear on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes the Board the ERISA 'administrator' while 1.1 allows a separate 'Administrator', a modest but visible overlap of roles.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition refers to the 'Internal Revenue Code of 1936', a date error for the 1986 Code that on its face defines the governing statute wrongly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 2.3, 4.4 and 10.1 rely on Code sections 401(a), 404 and 501(a), which exist under the 1986 Code, so the definition sits awkwardly with the provisions that use it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'other written agreement between an Employer and the Union, which is ... acceptable to the Board' leaves 'acceptable to the Board' as an unbounded qualifier on which agreements count.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.4(a) instead speaks of a CBA 'approved by the Board', and Section 9.1 makes the CBAs govern the rate of contribution, so the gate-keeping standard is stated two ways.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long definition that also carries substantive liability-shifting and incorporation-by-reference language 'to the extent not inconsistent with the terms of this Agreement'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with 5.5(h) (power to pool in Collective Trusts) and 1.22; the incorporation carve-out is a standard reconciliation device rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A Committee must contain 'at least one Employer Trustee and one Union Trustee' — plain and testable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.6(b) requires 'two or more Trustees ... an equal number of Employer Trustees and Union Trustees', a stricter parity rule than this definition's minimum.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Covered Employee' is tied to coverage under a CBA requiring contributions; a bounded definition, though 'covered under the terms of' does some unexamined work.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble's 'certain employees of the Employers' and 2.4(c)'s 'categories of employment of Covered Employees' overlay this definition without contradicting it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition points to 'Corporate Trustee' 'as that term is defined in Section 3.12', but 3.12 only uses the term without defining it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.12 treats the Corporate Trustee as a separate sole trustee while 1.12 folds it into 'Custodian', which is used throughout Articles 5 and 8 in a different, custodial sense.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any employer required to contribute ... pursuant to a Collective Bargaining Agreement' is definite in form, but its present-tense 'required to contribute' says nothing about employers whose obligation has ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble defines 'Employers' by Association membership plus contributing employers, and Article 9 (especially 9.5 and 9.10) imposes duties on 'delinquent' and withdrawing employers, so the scope of 'Employer' after withdrawal is not settled by the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference definition to Section 3.3(a); nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.3 was replaced by Amendment No. 4, but the cross-reference still functions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard statutory definition of ERISA including rules and regulations; no ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the many ERISA references throughout Articles 2, 5, 8 and 9.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines Foreign Securities entirely by reference to ERISA § 404(b) and 29 C.F.R. § 2550.404b-1; definite though wholly external.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in 1.21(h) and 5.5(p); no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'written communications signed by an Authorized Person' is then expanded to telex or 'any other such system' where identity can be verified 'with a reasonable degree of certainty', a soft boundary around what counts as signed writing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.2(a) and 8.6(a) rely on Instructions from Investment Managers, consistent with this definition; no contradiction located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but structured definition with three enumerated qualifying categories; the closing sentence permitting appointment of the Custodian as Investment Manager is a substantive power tucked into a definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That sentence interacts with 8.1 and with 8.5's disclaimer of Board responsibility for Investment Managers, and with 1.12's Custodian definition, but the pieces can be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines the Investment Manager Account as the segregated portion of the Fund; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.1(b) requires the Board (or Custodian) to segregate accounts while this definition says the Trustees segregate — a trivial difference of actor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Plan' means the detailed rules adopted by the Board; internally clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble uses 'Fund' and 'Plan' interchangeably, and 1.22 defines 'Fund' as assets, so the two labels are used inconsistently across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An eleven-item enumerated list opened by 'including, but not limited to' and closed by catch-all (k), the classic setting for an ejusdem generis argument about the catch-all's reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.5 grants investment powers over 'Securities or other property', so the breadth of this definition matters but does not contradict any other clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines Trust/Trust Fund/Fund as the assets held; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble and recitals use 'Fund' as a synonym for 'Plan', and 5.5(w) carves out monies that 'shall not be deemed plan assets of the Fund', so the term is not used uniformly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical '(if such Successor Trustees have been appointed ...)' awkwardly conditions the inclusion of successors and assigns.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 3.9, 3.10 and 3.11 govern successors consistently; the definition adds nothing contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'and any affiliates thereof' is an open-ended extension of the defined party without any test for affiliation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble uses the same collective formulation, and 1.8/1.11 make CBAs 'with the Union' the trigger for coverage, so affiliate status could matter but nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference to Section 3.3(b); nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.3 was replaced by Amendment No. 4, but the cross-reference still operates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line naming provision; nothing capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the preamble, the recitals and 9.3's payee designation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'certain pension and related benefits' leaves 'related benefits' undefined, and the exclusive-purpose formula sits against that open category.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.1(a) permits 'such other related benefits as the Board may from time to time determine', and the fourth recital speaks of 'pension and retirement benefits' only, so the purpose is stated at three different widths.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause declares that anything inconsistent with the Code or ERISA means 'this Agreement shall be deemed amended in such fashion as will implement the purposes of this Trust', a self-executing amendment of indeterminate content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overrides every other provision ('Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained herein') and cuts against Article 10's amendment procedure requiring a unanimous Board vote.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any contributing Employer acceptable to the Trustees may participate' with three enumerated steps; 'acceptable to the Trustees' is unstandardised but the mechanics are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.8 uses 'acceptable to the Board' for the underlying agreement while this uses 'acceptable to the Trustees' and 'approved by the Board' — three formulations of the same gate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deeming language ('shall be deemed to have ... agreed to be bound unconditionally') binds an employer to the whole Agreement and 'all of the decisions of the Trustees' without limit, and subparagraph (d) adds 'or other document, or as may be required by law'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the hook by which Article 9's interest and liquidated-damage terms (9.4, 9.5(b)) reach employers, while 9.1 says nothing in the Trust Agreement shall change the terms of the CBA — a real tension over what an employer has agreed to.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision plainly says two Employer Trustees and three Union Trustees; the words themselves are unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That 2-3 composition cannot be reconciled with Section 6.3's quorum of two Union and two Employer Trustees, 10.1(c)'s bar on unequal voting power, or 2.3's 'jointly-administered' LMRA § 302(c) requirement, and Amendment No. 4 rewrites it to 2-2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional acceptance-of-trusteeship clause; nothing vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches Section 3.4's written-acceptance requirement and the signature block; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare list of five named individuals; nothing to construe in the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It designates three Union Trustees, matching 3.1 as written but conflicting with 6.3's quorum and with Amendment No. 4's replacement naming only two per side.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'as soon as practicable after the appointments' is a soft timing standard, but the obligation is otherwise clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with 3.9, 3.10 and 3.11 (which key vesting to the filing of a written acceptance) without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Term runs until 'death, incapacity, resignation or removal as herein provided' — a short closed list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.6's deemed resignation and 3.8's removal by operation of law fit within the list; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentence deems a Trustee resigned when 'the Contributing Employer which designated him' ceases to contribute, a trigger that presupposes employer-level designation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 3.1, 3.3 and 3.7 make the Association (not any individual Contributing Employer) the designating body for Employer Trustees, so the deemed-resignation trigger has no counterpart in the appointment machinery.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Removal 'at any time, with or without cause' by written instrument of the Association; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits 3.9's successor mechanism and contrasts deliberately with 3.8's treatment of Union Trustees; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Headed 'Removal of Union Trustees' but the text is really an eligibility rule, and it says a successor shall be 'elected from the full-time officers' though the trustees are ex officio the union's three named officers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.10 says the Union's principal officer 'shall designate' a successor and then adds that the successor 'shall be elected', and Amendment No. 4 reduces the ex officio slate to two, so the appointment mechanism is stated inconsistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear filing mechanism for successor Employer Trustees.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.7 and 3.11; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause says the principal officer 'shall designate a successor ... by filing', then adds 'in which case a Successor Union Trustee shall be elected from the full-time officers' — designation and election stated as the same act.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.8 (and its Amendment No. 4 replacement) makes Union Trustees ex officio incumbents, which sits uneasily with both designation and election here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Successor Trustees vest with all powers 'as if originally named as Trustee'; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.4, 3.9 and 3.10; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subsection (c) is broken mid-sentence ('Notwithstanding such transfer, the Board ... functions under the Plan'), and (d) is likewise garbled, so the scope of the Trustees' release from liability is left textually incomplete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.12 defines 'Custodian' as a Corporate Trustee 'as that term is defined in Section 3.12', but this section never defines it and treats the Corporate Trustee as a sole trustee of a separate trust, which sits oddly with 5.12 and 5.5(n)(3).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The benefit limit is circular — 'no benefits other than pension, retirement, and such other related benefits as the Board may from time to time determine' — so the enumerated specifics are swallowed by an open-ended catch-all the Board itself defines.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2's exclusive purpose and the fourth recital's 'pension and retirement benefits' state the permitted scope more narrowly, and 5.14 gives the Board sole discretion to construe; the pieces can be harmonised but pull apart at the edges.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite: the Plan sets out eligibility and payment, and the Board may amend, modify or terminate it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10.1 conditions amendment of 'this Agreement and the Plan' on a unanimous Board vote and three provisos, and 10.2 forbids certain amendments outright, so the unqualified power stated here does not sit flush with Article 10.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence permitting the Plan to consist of insurance contracts; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.1(b), 5.4 and 5.3(a)(iv); no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The (a)/(b)/(c) triggers are transposed in the text — the clause about deductibility appears after the operative 'then' — so the conditions for returning a contribution cannot be read off the provision as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10.2 forbids any 'return or diversion of any part of the Fund to any of the Contributing Employers' and 10.3(b) says 'under no circumstances', while this clause authorises exactly such a return.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The anti-alienation text is fragmented and the last sentence lets the Board 'terminate or postpone' payments 'to the spouse, children and relatives of the person', which does not follow from the preceding restrictions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It carves out QDROs consistent with the Plan and ERISA, and 12.15 similarly denies any interest until the Board determines entitlement; no direct contradiction beyond the internal garble.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Board is 'vested with all right, title, and interest in and to such monies' — strong words for a trustee, but the trust purpose is stated in the same sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits 5.12 (deposit with Custodians), 9.3 and 2.2's exclusive-benefit purpose; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Benefits are paid 'at the time or times and in the manner specified in the Plan'; entirely referential and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches 4.1(b) and 4.2; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A seven-item list introduced by 'including, but not limited to' and governed by 'all reasonable and necessary expenses', leaving the outer edge of chargeable expenses open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.2(8) cross-refers to 'expenses of the type set forth in Sections 5.3 and 5.5(n)', and 5.3(d) bars trustee compensation while allowing reimbursement — consistent readings are available.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long, carefully structured insurance-contract provision with clear allocations of authority and non-party status for insurers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.3, 5.3(b) and 10.3(c); no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Twenty-five enumerated powers closing with (y), 'Generally, perform all acts (whether or not expressly authorized herein) which the Trustees may deem necessary and prudent' — the paradigm general-catch-all-against-enumerated-specifics problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.4(a) purports to withhold from Investment Managers 'subsections (3) through (y)' of this section, a cross-reference that does not match the lettering, and 5.7 imposes a prudence standard on the same powers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'including but not limited to' responsibilities related to benefit applications and delinquent contributions leaves the delegable set open, but the parity rule in (b) is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.10 requires only 'at least one Employer Trustee and one Union Trustee' whereas 5.6(b) demands an equal number of each, and 7.2(9) contemplates a 'separate delinquency committee'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A verbatim restatement of ERISA's prudent-person and diversification standards, including the 'unless clearly prudent not to do so' proviso; standard and well-understood.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the 'sole and absolute discretion' language in 5.5 and 5.14, which is a normal limit rather than a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reliance protection for instruments 'believed by them to be genuine' and for professional opinions relied on 'in good faith'; conventional and bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with 4.1(b)-(c) and 5.9; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing words 'except as may otherwise reimbursed by insurance' drop a verb, and (b)'s blanket protection against 'any error of judgment or ... any act or omission' is broader than (d)'s good-faith and gross-negligence carve-outs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The opening 'Except as may otherwise be provided by ERISA' reconciles it with 5.7's fiduciary standard and 5.11's insurance, so the tension is largely internal to the section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Bonding is pegged to ERISA § 412 amounts with a discretionary power to require more; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Costs are payable from the Fund, consistent with 5.3(a); no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To the extent not precluded by ERISA, the Fund shall purchase and maintain' fiduciary insurance — a mandatory obligation with a statutory qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly ties back to 5.9's indemnity obligations and 5.3(a)(iv); no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deposit and signature-authority mechanics stated with precision, including the two-Trustee bipartisan signing rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with 5.1, 5.15 and 1.12's Custodian definition; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'ministerial powers or duties' is the operative limit, and the line between ministerial and fiduciary functions is not drawn anywhere in the instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.6(a) allows delegation of 'fiduciary responsibilities' to Committees and 5.5(r) allows delegation of Plan-operation duties 'other than Trustee duties', so three different delegation standards coexist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'complete authority, in its sole and absolute discretion, to construe the terms of the Plan or this Agreement' with decisions 'final and binding upon all parties affected' is the sort of reservation-of-discretion language parties routinely fight over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is hard to square with 6.6 and 9.10, which send deadlocks and withdrawal-liability disputes to binding arbitration, and with 9.7's contemplation of judicial awards.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Execution authority is allocated to named officers and to bipartisan groups, with a clear third-party reliance rule; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.6 makes instruments executed by the Chairman alone conclusive, a slightly wider rule than the Chairman-and-Secretary formula here and in 1.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The term of Fund officers shall commence on the date of their election and continues until their successors are elected' — a tense slip, but the meaning is not in doubt.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Chairman must be a Union Trustee and the Secretary an Employer Trustee, which fits 6.6(a)'s Chairman role and 5.15; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Paragraph (b) lets 'any four Trustees' call a special meeting, and (c) permits telephone meetings 'with proper advance notice (as prescribed by either paragraph (a) or (b))' though (a) prescribes no notice at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: With five Trustees under 3.1 (and only four after Amendment No. 4), the 'any four Trustees' threshold collides with 3.1 and with 6.3's quorum of four, effectively requiring the whole Board.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A quorum of two Union and two Employer Trustees is arithmetically precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Under Section 3.1 there are only two Employer Trustees, so the quorum silently requires every Employer Trustee, and after Amendment No. 4's 2-2 board a quorum means full attendance — an awkward fit with 6.4(c)'s proxy scheme and 6.4(d)'s 'lack of a quorum' contingency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It says action shall be 'by unanimous vote of the Trustees' and then that action is 'by unanimous vote of the two units', two different things, and (b) requires 'a majority of all the Union Trustees' which cannot be achieved on a two-member unit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1's 2-3 split and Amendment No. 4's 2-2 split each strain the unit-majority rule, and 6.3's quorum plus 6.6's arbitration backstop must be read together with (d).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Minutes must be maintained but 'need not be verbatim' — a light obligation, plainly stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 11.1(b)'s recordkeeping duties; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Chairman 'shall submit' the question on any Trustee's request but the deadlock definition ('lack of a unanimous vote', quorum failure at two successive meetings) and the (e) reference to 'both parties' in a five-trustee body leave the trigger imprecise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.4(d) states the arbitration trigger in partly different terms, and 9.10 creates a separate arbitration regime, so the instrument contains two arbitration clauses of different scope.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening sentence is broken — 'Where the Administrator is a Trust Fund, subject to the terms of this Agreement ...' has no predicate — so the section never states what the Administrator is actually responsible for.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.1 makes the Administrator the Board or its delegate and 1.6 makes the Board the ERISA 'administrator', so who bears these listed functions depends on a sentence that is missing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An eighteen-item list of responsibilities ending in a general catch-all ('Generally, exercise of those functions ... which the Board deems necessary and appropriate'), with items (1) and (2) asserting a right to amend or terminate 'at any time'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Items (1)-(2) conflict with Section 10.1's unanimity requirement and provisos and with 10.2's flat prohibition on certain amendments, and item (5) carves out functions delegated under 5.6, 7.1 and Article 8.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear appointment and segregation mechanics; '(c)' contains the typo 'the Securities of other property' but the sense is obvious.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates 8.4(b) almost exactly on the Board's residual power, a redundancy rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Appointment by certificate, written duties, and periodic review — precise and procedural.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with 1.18, 8.3 and 8.8's guidelines; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Board 'may require' the acknowledgment, whereas the qualifying certificate is what defines the manager; permissive but clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.18 defines 'Investment Manager' as one who 'has acknowledged in writing' fiduciary status, which reads as mandatory against this section's 'may require'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exception 'except subsections (3) through (y)' cannot be right — Section 5.5 has no subsection (3) — so the range of powers withheld from an Investment Manager is not determinable from the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The defect only matters by reference to Section 5.5's lettering (a) through (y), and 8.4(b)/8.1(c) state the Board's residual authority twice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad 'Notwithstanding anything to the contrary' disclaimer of Board liability, with a carve-out for assets over which it 'has specifically assumed investment management duties'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read against 5.7's prudence standard, 7.2(13)'s monitoring duty and 8.2(c)'s periodic review obligation — the disclaimer sits in tension with duties expressly imposed elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Order-placement authority stated plainly and subordinated to the investment management agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 8.4(a) and 8.8; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence making appointment terms 'the sole responsibility of the Board'; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits alongside 8.5's disclaimer of Board liability for the manager's acts, a juxtaposition that is odd but reconcilable (selection versus performance).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Guidelines 'may (but need not)' be issued, and issuing them 'shall not in any manner be construed as an acceptance' of management powers; deliberately drafted and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors 8.5 and 7.2(10); no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The last sentence — 'Nothing in this Trust Agreement shall be deemed to change, alter or amend any of the terms or provisions of any such agreement' — is a broad subordination clause whose reach is not defined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is difficult to reconcile with 9.4(b) and 9.5(b), which impose liquidated damages and 18% interest not found in the CBAs, and with 2.5's deeming of employers bound to all provisions of this Agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Effective date and duration of the contribution obligation are keyed entirely to the CBA; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.1 and 1.13; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Payee and 'manner and form prescribed by the Board' — a simple mechanical rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.9's remittance-report requirement; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'a liquidated damage penalty equal to the greater of interest on, or twenty percent of, the unpaid contributions' calls the same sum both liquidated damages and a penalty, and (a)'s 'interest, at a rate calculated in accordance with Section 9.5' assumes 9.5 supplies a rate calculation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.5 contains no calculation method, only a flat 18% listed among recoverable 'expenses', and 9.7(b)-(c) again refers to 'the method set forth in Section 9.5' — the cross-references do not find what they point at.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 18% figure is buried inside a list of 'expenses incurred in effectuating such payment', so whether it is a substantive interest rate or merely a recoverable cost item, and what payments it attaches to, is genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 9.4(a) and 9.7(b)-(c) treat 9.5 as supplying a rate 'method' for unpaid contributions, while Article 9 is headed 'Payments to the Fund' and only 9.10 addresses withdrawal liability — leaving it unresolved whether the 18% reaches withdrawal-liability payments at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The defined shorthand 'unpaid contributions' is assembled from contributions required by this Agreement, any CBA 'or other agreement', and 'any rules or guidelines promulgated by the Board' — an open-ended set given a defined-term label.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That same term is then used in 9.7(a)-(c) to fix the judgment amount, so its breadth here determines the reach of the remedies there, and 9.5(b)/9.10 use a different vocabulary for withdrawal liability.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subsections (b) and (c) both compute interest 'in accordance with the method set forth in Section 9.5', a method that section does not set out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.5(b) states only a flat rate as an expense item and Amendment No. 2 makes even that rate discretionary, so the computation this clause depends on is supplied nowhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Nothing in this Article IX shall be construed as a waiver' preserves rights 'in any other type of proceeding' — a broad, undefined saving of remedies (and it mixes roman and arabic article numbering).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.10 says withdrawal-liability claims 'shall not become the subject of litigation in the courts ... but shall be subject to determination only by arbitration', which is hard to square with this open preservation of other proceedings.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'all records deemed necessary by such persons' and 'The Board may charge an Employer for the cost of conducting an audit' leave both the scope of the audit and the charge without any standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits 5.3(a)'s payment of collection expenses and 7.2(7)'s auditor coordination; no direct contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It makes arbitration the only forum for 'any and all claims by third parties (including Employers) ... concerning the assessment ... of withdrawal liability', then preserves the Fund's right to sue for 'any amount demanded' if the claimant does not timely arbitrate — a one-sided asymmetry a court could be asked to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.8 preserves enforcement 'in any other type of proceeding' and 9.5(a) authorises 'whatever action or proceedings may be proper', both of which pull against this exclusive-arbitration command.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Amendment 'at any time and in any manner' is then hedged by three provisos, one of which — 'not inconsistent with the purposes for which the Fund was established' — is an open standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.2(1)-(2) states an unqualified right to amend or terminate 'at any time' and 4.2 lets the Board amend the Plan without the provisos, while the sixth recital points to a non-existent 'Paragraph 18'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat prohibition on diverting the Fund, with a single carve-out 'except as otherwise provided in Section 10.3'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10.3(b) contains no exception at all — it says 'under no circumstances' shall the corpus revert to an Employer — so the carve-out points to a provision that does not supply one, while 4.4 does allow returns to Employers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'automatically, in the event that the obligation of all Employers to make contributions ... shall terminate' is a self-executing trigger with no notice or determination mechanism, and (b) leaves surplus distribution to what is 'consistent, in their opinion' with the Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsection (b)'s 'under no circumstances shall any portion ... revert or accrue to the benefit of any Employer' contradicts Section 4.4's power to return mistaken or non-deductible contributions and leaves 10.2's 'except as provided in Section 10.3' with nothing to refer to.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Recordkeeping duties stated with precision, including annual examination by a CPA and inspection rights 'at all reasonable times'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The opening 'Unless otherwise delegated' meshes with 5.13, 5.6 and 7.1(g); no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Valuation at 'fair market value, computed in accordance with such commercially acceptable valuation method or methods determined by the Board' is circular — the Board picks the method and the standard is its own good faith.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies 'for all purposes of this Agreement' and so interacts with 11.1(c) and 5.5(v)'s collateral tests, but I found no provision it contradicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'a principal office in the New York City metropolitan area' is a soft geographic boundary, and the Board 'shall be deemed to be located at that address' though no address is given.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 12.8 and its amendments give specific Long Island City addresses, which fall within the described area; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard New York choice-of-law clause with an express ERISA-preemption qualifier; carefully drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.10 separately provides that withdrawal-liability arbitrations 'shall be governed by New York State Law to the extent not superceded by ERISA', a consistent restatement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ordinary counterparts clause; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Section 3.2's reference to signature on 'any counterpart or copy'; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Headings are for convenience only and 'this Agreement shall not be construed by reference to them'; the plural/gender rules are conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This matters for provisions whose headings do not match their text (notably 3.8 and 5.14), but it resolves rather than creates tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence designating the Board as agent for service; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 12.1's situs and 12.8's notice addresses; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It makes every instrument 'executed by the Chairman of the Trustees' conclusive on three enumerated points in favour of third parties — a strong, one-sided protection but clearly bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 1.4 and 5.15 contemplate execution by the Chairman and Secretary together (or by resolution), so the Chairman-alone conclusiveness rule here is broader than the execution authority granted elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All words and phrases defined in the Plan shall have the same meaning in this Agreement, except as otherwise expressly provided' imports an external document's definitions wholesale.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 1 defines the same core terms ('Plan', 'Covered Employee', 'Employer') and its preface adds 'unless the context otherwise requires', so two definitional hierarchies operate on the same words.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Notice is 'deemed duly given when either delivered in writing ... or when deposited by first-class mail', and the final sentence about the date of receipt is cut off mid-phrase; the Union address also reads 41-18 rather than 47-18.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendments Nos. 1 and 3 replace these addresses and rename the addressee 'Fund Director', a title used nowhere else in the instrument (compare the defined 'Administrator' in 1.1).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text begins mid-sentence ('the Board) or any person claiming by or through them'), so the class of persons denied any interest cannot be identified from the provision itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be read with 12.16 and with 4.5's anti-alienation rule and 5.14's determination authority; the missing opening makes that reconciliation guesswork.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional no-employment-right and no-equity clause, closing with 'except as set forth in the Plan'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels 12.15 and defers to the Plan, consistently with 4.2 and 5.2; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Perpetual duration 'subject, however, to the provisions ... set forth in Article 10'; short and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 10.3(a)(3) provides for automatic termination, which this clause expressly accommodates; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The amendment says 'the Plan is hereby amended' while the operative change is to Section 12.8(b) of the Trust Agreement — the wrong instrument is named.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It substitutes 'Fund Director' for 'Fund Administrator' without amending Article 1, leaving an undefined title alongside the defined 'Administrator' in 1.1 and 7.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The replacement text adds '18 percent per annum or such other interest rate that the Trustees deem appropriate given the circumstances', which converts a fixed rate into an open-ended discretionary one with no standard or cap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 9.4(a) and 9.7(b)-(c) compute interest 'in accordance with the method set forth in Section 9.5', and a rate the Trustees may set at will is not a 'method', so the cross-referring provisions are left without a determinate measure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A straightforward address substitution, though the Association address text is truncated after '620 Eighth Avenue'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It continues the 'Fund Director' label introduced by Amendment No. 1 rather than the defined 'Administrator' of Section 1.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The restated preamble carries a stray '2. the following:' line and again equates 'Fund' with 'Plan', but the substance — the four named Trustees — is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces the original preamble's five Trustees and matches Amendment No. 4's 2-2 composition, but the Fund/Plan equation still conflicts with the separate definitions in 1.20 and 1.22.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing sentence reads 'The appointment of Trustees shall be selected by the provisions of Section 3.4', a plain drafting error for 'governed by'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The new 2-2 composition means Section 6.3's quorum (two Union and two Employer Trustees) requires the entire Board, and 6.2(b)'s 'any four Trustees' now means unanimity to call a special meeting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare list of four names replacing Section 3.3; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the amended 3.1 and the amended preamble; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Headed 'Removal of Union Trustees' but the text is an ex officio eligibility rule, and it says a successor 'shall be elected from the full-time officers' even though the two seats are tied to named offices.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.10 (unamended) still says the Union's principal officer 'shall designate' the successor, so designation and election remain stated as alternatives for the same act.
